segments: 282 Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
Amir Ilghazi, son of Artuq, [went] to Harran,
and bound the notable elders who were in it, and its judge.
And in this year,
which is the year 1430 {OCR: ܐܬܠ for ܐܬܠ = 1430},
1430 of the Greeks [1119 AD],
although the lord of Aleppo gave much gold to Roger, the lord of Antioch,
he was only able to make peace with him for four months,
until they gathered the harvest
and stored {lit. hung up} the threshing floors.
Then Roger came and encamped against Aleppo,
and the people of Aleppo took refuge with Amir Ilghazi, son of Artuq, the lord of Mardin.
And he gathered seven thousand Turks,
and came and met the Franks and crushed them,
and this Prince Roger was killed in the battle.
And those of the Franks who were saved from the battle fled to Antioch.
And the Turks took control over the region of Antioch,
and they killed a multitude of monks on the Black Mountain,
until Baldwin (the Second), the king of Jerusalem, heard [of it]
and pursued the Turks.
And when the ambush of the Turks destroyed some of the Frankish foot-soldiers,
King Baldwin turned back against them
and wiped them all out.
And again he turned and pursued Ilghazi,
and rescued the spoil from the hands of the Turks and entered Antioch.
The blessed Mar Michael says
that Ghazi, son of Danishmand, crushed the Franks
and killed Roger;
and perhaps the similarity of the name was the cause of the error.
And in this year, the Sultan of Melitene subdued the region of Jihan and Albistan,
and took control over the fortress of Qati'a.
And in the month of Shebat of this year, the Franks raided the region of Melitene,
and the Turks [raided] the region of Gargar.
And the Sultan of Melitene raided the region of Kamakha,
and its lord went and took refuge with the Greeks of Trebizond,
and Gabras came with him.
And the Sultan and Balak met the Greeks
and defeated them.
And Gabras was captured,
and he ransomed himself again for thirty thousand dinars,
and went to his country.
And John, the king of Constantinople, took three fortresses from the Turks.
And Ilghazi burned the crops of the region of Edessa,
and also raided the region of Antioch.
And Toghtekin, the lord of Damascus, died.
And when his son sat in his place,
a certain Turk whose name was Altuntash attacked him and killed him,
and he ruled over Damascus.
And in the year 515 {OCR: ܬܩܝܗ},
515 of the Arabs [1121/1122 AD],
Malik rebelled
